home.title: Admin
home.loadFailed: This page couldn't load everything. <link>Open System</link> for the details.
home.loadFailedSchema: This page couldn't load everything. It needs the database update described above. <link>Open System</link> for the details.
home.subtitle: Everything about your platform: branding, resellers, payments, AI and the people using it.
home.appsDomainTitle: Give apps their own web address
home.appsDomainBody: Published apps currently run on the studio's own address. Because other people build apps here, set <mono>APPS_DOMAIN</mono> (for example <mono>myapps.site</mono>, with a wildcard DNS record <mono>*.myapps.site</mono> pointing at this server) so every app runs on its own address and can never reach the studio or other apps. The installer can do this for you.
home.statPaidUsersHelp: People on any plan other than Free, whether they pay through Stripe or you set the plan by hand.
home.statFlowsHelp: Workflows: automated steps people have set up in their apps, like sending an email when a form is filled in.
home.statFlowRunsHelp: How many times workflows have run, as far back as the saved run logs go.
home.funnelBody: How quickly people who sign up get an app live. Measured from sign-up to their first published app.
home.cameWithIdeaHelp: People who signed up after typing an app idea into the box on the home page.
home.medianTimeHelp: The typical time from signing up to publishing a first app: half of people are quicker, half slower.
home.usersHelp: Everyone with an account, newest 50 first. Change someone's plan, send a password link, open their workspace to help them, or delete them.
home.recentRunsHelp: The latest 20 times any workflow ran. A status in the 200s (green) means it worked; anything else (red) means it failed.
home.refusedIntro: Apps the platform refused to build or change because they are similar to NullKode LLC’s own products. Nothing was charged for them.
home.refusedHelp: Every request the build rule refused, newest first: in the studio, the Designer, Ask AI and the partner API. You can turn the rule off in Settings → AI.
home.refusedWhereHelp: What was asked (a new plan, a change, a build, an Ask AI edit, a Designer change) and what gave it away (fixed patterns, the AI check, the plan, the images or the result).

schema.values: {count, plural, one {# list value} other {# list values}}
schema.both: {columns, plural, one {# column} other {# columns}} and {values, plural, one {# list value} other {# list values}}
schema.title: The database is missing {what}; the site will fail until it is updated.
schema.fix: Back up the database, then run <mono>pnpm exec prisma db push</mono> in the app folder and restart the app. Docker installs do this by themselves when the app restarts (<mono>docker compose up -d</mono>).

impersonate.label: Impersonate
impersonate.confirm: Impersonate {email}? Everything you do will happen as them.
impersonate.help: See the studio exactly as this person does, to help them. Anything you change happens in their account. Use the bar at the top of the page to switch back.

users.planHelp: Changes their plan straight away. It doesn't charge them or change any Stripe subscription, and a later payment update from Stripe can switch it back.
users.linkCopied: Link copied. Send it to them; it works once for 2 hours.
users.passwordLinkHelp: Makes a one-time link for them to choose a new password, valid for 2 hours. It's emailed to them if email is on; otherwise it's copied for you to send.
users.deleteHelp: Permanently deletes their account and all their apps, data and files, cancelling any subscription first. You'll see what goes before you confirm. Can't be undone.
users.isReseller: They run the reseller workspace “{name}”. Remove it under Admin, Resellers first, then delete the account.
users.isSelf: This is your own account. Use Delete my account on your Profile page.
users.billingHandled: I've cancelled their subscription in the payment dashboard myself.
users.deleteNone: This deletes their account. They have no apps.
users.deleteOne: This deletes their account and their app, with everything the app saved and its files.
users.deleteMany: This deletes their account and all {count} of their apps, with everything the apps saved and their files.
users.keysAckOne: One app has a Google Play upload key. Only the app's owner can download it. I understand it will be lost, and the owner could never update that app on Google Play again.
users.keysAckMany: {count} apps have a Google Play upload key. Only the app's owner can download it. I understand it will be lost, and the owner could never update that app on Google Play again.

controlPanel.brandText: Your name, logo, browser icon, colours and help email. Shown on every studio page, email and sign-in screen.
controlPanel.resellersText: Agencies that sell app building to their own customers under their own brand, domain and Stripe account.
controlPanel.resellersStatus: {resellers, plural, one {# reseller} other {# resellers}} · {clients, plural, one {# client} other {# clients}}
controlPanel.resellersNone: None yet. Add your first reseller
controlPanel.paymentsText: Connect your Stripe account and set the price of each paid plan. Customers pay you directly.
controlPanel.paymentsStatus: Stripe connected · {count, plural, one {# paid plan} other {# paid plans}}
controlPanel.paymentsNone: Not connected. Everyone is on the Free plan
controlPanel.plansText: What Free, Starter, Pro and Team include: apps, published apps, pages, own domains and AI actions.
controlPanel.aiText: Which AI builds apps and makes edits: a hosted service or a model running on your own server.
controlPanel.aiNone: Not set up. Building with AI is off
controlPanel.emailText: Send invitations, password links and app alerts from your own address, through any email provider.
controlPanel.emailNone: Not set up. Links are shown on screen instead
controlPanel.usersText: Change anyone's plan, send a password link, or open their workspace to help them.
controlPanel.systemText: Server health in plain words: database, disk space, scheduled flows, backups, nightly clean-up and recent errors.
controlPanel.systemRed: {count, plural, one {# problem needs attention} other {# problems need attention}}
controlPanel.systemAmber: Working · {count, plural, one {# thing to look at} other {# things to look at}}
controlPanel.stepStripe: Connect Stripe and price your plans
controlPanel.stepEmail: Turn on email so invites, password links and app alerts are sent for you
controlPanel.stepApps: Give published apps their own address (APPS_DOMAIN)
controlPanel.stepAppsHelp: Gives every published app its own web address, kept apart from the studio. It's set in the server's settings file (.env), not on this screen.
controlPanel.heading: Run your platform
controlPanel.checklistHelp: The main steps to get your platform ready for customers. Each one ticks itself off once it's set up; click a step to go to its setting.
controlPanel.appsDomainNote: The apps address is a server setting: add it to the <mono>.env</mono> file (the installer can do it) and restart.
controlPanel.how1: 1. You run the platform and set the plans, prices and limits.
controlPanel.how2: 2. Resellers are agencies you add under Resellers. You choose how many clients, apps and AI actions each one gets.
controlPanel.how3: 3. App owners are the reseller's clients. They sign in at the reseller's own domain and only ever see the reseller's name, logo and colours.
controlPanel.how4: 4. App users use the published apps on the web, as an installable app, or on Android and iPhone.
controlPanel.howNote: Each reseller gets their own dashboard for branding, their domain, their Stripe account and their clients. Clients pay the reseller directly; the platform takes no cut.

business.title: Payments
business.help: Set your prices and connect Stripe, the card payment service. Your direct customers pay straight into your own Stripe account.
business.body: Your prices, and the Stripe account customers pay. Resellers set their own prices for their clients.

brandSettings.title: White-label branding
brandSettings.help: White-label means your own name, logo and colours are shown everywhere instead of the platform's defaults.
brandSettings.body: Your platform's name, logo, browser icon, colours and help email. Everyone who isn't a reseller's client sees these. Resellers set their own brand in their dashboard.
brandSettings.saved: Saved. Everyone sees the new branding on their next page.

settings.aiHelp: Chooses the AI that builds new apps and makes edits for everyone on the platform, including resellers and their clients.
settings.aiSubtitle: Pick which engine builds new apps and answers in-editor edits.
settings.openaiHelp: Use OpenAI, or an AI service or model on your own server that works the same way (OpenAI-compatible). You'll set its address, model name and usually a secret key.
settings.openaiDescription: OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible server, including local models. Set the endpoint and model below.
settings.cliHelp: Use a command-line AI tool installed on this server and signed in to its own subscription, instead of paying per use with a secret key.
settings.cliDescription: Uses a locally installed, signed-in CLI subscription instead of per-token API billing.
settings.apiKeyHelp: The secret key from your AI provider's account. It's kept hidden; leave the box empty to keep the key already saved.
settings.apiKeySet: A key is configured. Enter a new value to replace it, or leave blank to keep the current one.
settings.apiKeyNone: No key configured — add one or set OPENAI_API_KEY in .env.
settings.baseUrlHelp: The web address of your AI service. Leave it empty to use OpenAI itself, or enter your own server's address to use a model you run yourself.
settings.baseUrlHint: Empty = OpenAI. Local server example: http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1
settings.jsonSupportHelp: How strictly the AI is asked to answer in the fixed format the builder reads. If builds fail with format errors on your AI service, try a looser option.
settings.jsonSupportHint: Use JSON mode for compatible servers; text mode if JSON mode is unsupported.
settings.contextSizeHelp: How much text the model can read at once. Leave it empty to detect it automatically. Small models get shorter instructions so they still work.
settings.contextSizeHint: Leave blank to detect it automatically (use Test connection to see the result). Models under 24K get compact prompts.
settings.thinkingHelp: Whether a “thinking” model may reason at length before it answers. Off is fastest; On may give better results but builds can take much longer.
settings.thinkingHint: Reasoning models (e.g. Qwen3) can spend minutes thinking before they answer. Automatic turns it off for local servers so builds stay fast.
settings.maxTokensHelp: Caps how long each AI reply can be (a token is roughly ¾ of a word). Leave it empty for no limit. Small models on your own server may need a cap.
settings.maxTokensHint: Leave blank for no limit. Set one (e.g. 8192) for small local models.
settings.scaffoldModelHelp: The exact model name used to build new apps from a description. Leave it empty for the default; for a service other than OpenAI you must enter it.
settings.editModelHelp: The exact model name used for AI edits in the page editor. Leave it empty for the default; for a service other than OpenAI you must enter it.
settings.testHelp: Saves the settings above, then sends a short test message to your AI service and shows whether it replied, how fast, and how much text the model can read.
settings.cliNote: The command-line AI tool must be installed on this server and signed in, once, as the user that runs this platform (or the dedicated runner account, if one is configured). See docs/deploy/plesk.md.
settings.cliModelHelp: Which model the command-line AI tool should use, by its short name or full ID.
settings.cliModelHint: The tool's short model name or full ID
settings.cliBinHelp: Where the command-line AI tool is installed on this server. Leave it empty to let the server find it by itself.
settings.cliTestHelp: Saves these settings, then checks that the command-line AI tool on this server starts, is signed in and replies.
settings.saveAiHelp: Saves the AI settings. They apply to everyone on the platform, including resellers and their clients.
settings.plansHelp: Sets what your direct customers get on each plan; resellers set their own for their clients. Lowering a limit never deletes anything, it only stops people adding more.
settings.plansSubtitle: What each plan includes. Tick unlimited for no limit. Reset returns a plan to the built-in defaults. You (and resellers) are never limited.

limitHelp.maxProjects: How many apps someone on this plan can have in total, live or not.
limitHelp.maxPublished: How many of their apps can be live on the web at the same time.
limitHelp.maxPagesPerProject: The most pages a single app can have.
limitHelp.maxCustomDomains: How many of their own web addresses (like shop.theirbusiness.com) they can connect, across all their apps.
limitHelp.aiActionsPerMonth: How many times a month they can ask the AI to build or change something. The count starts again each month.
limitHelp.scheduledFlows: Whether workflows can run on a timer, like every hour. Turning it off stops scheduled workflows on that plan from running.

settings.savePlansHelp: Saves the limits for all four plans. They apply to your direct customers straight away.
settings.resetHelp: Fills in the built-in standard limits. Nothing changes until you press Save plan limits.
settings.visionHelp: Whether the AI model can look at pictures. People can add reference images (concept art, sketches, screenshots) when they build an app; if the model can’t read them, they are refused with a clear message instead of being ignored.
settings.visionHint: Automatic knows the common models that can read images.
settings.buildPolicy: Refuse apps similar to NullKode LLC’s products
settings.buildPolicyHelp: When on, the AI won’t build or change apps that copy the NullKode platform, IgniteUps.ai or other AI tools made by NullKode LLC. Refusals are listed on the admin home page.
settings.buildPolicyHint: On by default. Checked on every plan, build, Ask AI edit and Designer change.

language.title: Language
language.help: The language the studio is shown in for people who haven't picked one themselves. Anyone can still choose their own language from the account menu.
language.body: The language new visitors and people who haven't chosen one see. Each person's own choice always wins; resellers can set a different default for their clients.
language.label: Default language

settingsPage.subtitle: Your brand, payments, email, AI engine and what each plan includes.

api.emailAddResendFrom: Add the address emails are sent from, on a domain you verified in Resend.
api.emailTestLimit: That's 5 test emails in the last hour. Please try again in {minutes} minutes.

email.saved: Saved. Invitations, password links and app alerts now use these settings.
email.testFailed: The test email couldn't be sent.
email.testSent: Sent to {to}. Check that inbox (and its spam folder).
email.testSentUnsaved: Sent to {to}. Check that inbox (and its spam folder). Save to start using these settings.
email.removeConfirm: Remove the saved email settings? Email then uses the server's settings file (.env) if it has any, or turns off.
email.title: Email
email.body: Send invitations, password links, app alerts and your apps' own emails from your address. Without email, links are shown on screen for you to pass on.
email.onResend: Email is on: sending through Resend from {from}.
email.onSmtp: Email is on: sending through your email server from {from}.
email.fromEnv: These come from the server's settings file (.env). Saving here takes over from it.
email.statsSkipped: {count} not sent because email was off
email.howHelp: SMTP means your email provider's sending settings; almost every provider has them. Resend is a sending service that uses a secret key instead.
email.smtpText: Works with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Brevo, Mailgun, Postmark, Amazon SES, Resend and most web hosts.
email.resendText: Send with a Resend API key. Your sender domain must be verified in Resend.
email.serverHint: Your provider lists it as the SMTP server or host.
email.portHint: Use 587 unless your provider says otherwise. Many hosting companies block port 25.
email.usernameHelp: The login for your email provider's sending settings, usually your full email address.
email.passwordSaved: Saved. Leave blank to keep it
email.passwordHint: Some providers (Google, Microsoft) need an app password instead of your normal one.
email.encryptionHelp: How the connection to your email server is kept private. Leave it on Automatic unless your email provider says otherwise.
email.resendKeyHelp: The secret key from your Resend account. It's kept hidden; leave the box empty to keep the key already saved.
email.resendKeySaved: Saved ({mask}). Leave blank to keep it
email.resendKeyEnv: Using the key in the server's settings file. Leave blank to keep it
email.fromHint: An address your provider lets you send from.
email.fromHintResend: An address your provider lets you send from, on a domain you verified in Resend.
email.senderNameHint: Leave blank to use your brand or the app's name on each email.
email.saveHelp: Saves these settings. From then on, invitations, password links and app alerts for everyone on the platform, resellers' clients included, are sent this way.
email.test: Send a test email to me
email.removeHelp: Deletes the email settings saved here. Email then uses the server's settings file (.env) if it has any, or turns off.
email.testNote: The test goes to {email}. It uses what's on screen, so you can check before saving.

system.title: System
system.subtitle: How the server is doing, in plain words. If something looks wrong, the details at the bottom help whoever supports you.
system.summaryRed: {red, plural, one {# problem needs attention now.} other {# problems need attention now.}}
system.summaryRedAmber: {red, plural, one {# problem needs} other {# problems need}} attention now, and {amber, plural, one {# thing} other {# things}} to look at.
system.summaryAmber: Everything important is working. {amber, plural, one {# thing} other {# things}} could use a look.
system.cleanupHelp: Tidies the database each night so it doesn't keep growing. Choose below whether it only reports what it would remove or actually removes old records.
system.runsAt: Runs once a day at {time} server time (NK_MAINTENANCE_HOUR). It keeps:
system.keepRuns: flow run logs for {days} days ({failedDays} for failed runs), at most {perFlow} per flow, and always each flow's latest run;
system.keepSessions: sign-ins until they expire, and invitation or password links until used or expired;
system.keepVersions: each app's newest {count} published versions, plus the live one and the one before it;
system.keepTrash: deleted apps' files and data for {days} days.
system.uploadsKept: Files people uploaded are never removed: pages and apps may still use them.
system.lastRemoved: {when}, removed {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} ({size}).
system.lastWouldRemove: {when}, would remove {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} ({size}).
system.stepsFailed: {count, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}} failed; see the recent errors below.
system.supportBody: Version {version}, {install} ({arch}). The details include the checks above, the names of the settings in your .env file (never their values) and the recent errors, with private data hidden.
system.errorsBodyOne: One so far since the server started, newest first. Email addresses, keys and passwords are hidden.
system.errorsBodyMany: The latest {count} since the server started, newest first. Email addresses, keys and passwords are hidden.

systemActions.copyHelp: Copies this page's checks, setting names and recent errors, with private data hidden, so you can paste them into a message to whoever supports you.
systemActions.downloadHelp: Saves the same details as a text file you can attach to a support request.
systemActions.bugHelp: Opens a new bug report for the platform's developers, with your version filled in. Paste the copied details into it and read them over before posting.
systemActions.copied: Copied. Paste it into your message or bug report.
systemActions.failed: That didn't work. Please try again.
systemActions.started: Started. It's still working; refresh this page in a few minutes to see the result.
systemActions.done: Done. The result is shown above.
systemActions.network: Check your connection and try again.
systemActions.applyConfirm: Turn on nightly clean-up? Old run logs, expired sign-ins, old published versions and deleted apps' files older than a week will be removed for good. Take a backup first if you want to keep them.

modeHelp.report: Each night, count what could be removed. Nothing is deleted.
modeHelp.apply: Each night, delete what the rules below allow. Deleted records can't be brought back.

systemActions.fromEnv: Currently set by NK_MAINTENANCE in the server's .env file. Saving here overrides it.
systemActions.runHelp: Runs the clean-up right away. Old records it finds are removed for good.
systemActions.checkHelp: Counts what the clean-up would remove, without deleting anything.

resellers.title: Resellers
resellers.intro: Resellers sell your platform under their own brand. Each gets a dashboard to invite clients, brand the experience, connect their own domain and bill clients on their own Stripe account. You set how many clients and apps each reseller can have.
resellers.aiNote: The monthly AI limit covers the reseller's clients and the reseller's own workspace together. When it runs out, AI pauses for all of them until the next month, and the reseller is emailed at 80% and 100% (when email is set up).
resellers.createdEmailed: Reseller created and invitation emailed. Link:
resellers.createdLink: Reseller created. Send them this link to set their password:
resellers.createdExisting: Reseller created. They can sign in with their existing password and will see the Reseller dashboard.
resellers.billingConfirm:
{error}

If you've cancelled their subscriptions in the reseller's Stripe dashboard yourself, press OK to delete the reseller anyway.
resellers.signInFailed: Couldn't sign in as this reseller.
resellers.addBodyEmail: New resellers get an invitation email. Leave a quota empty for unlimited.
resellers.addBodyLink: You'll get an invitation link to send them. Leave a quota empty for unlimited.
resellers.brandNameHelp: The reseller's business name. Their clients see it instead of yours; the reseller can change it later in their dashboard.
resellers.emailHelp: The reseller signs in with this. A new address gets an invitation; if it already has an account here, that account becomes a reseller.
resellers.maxClientsHelp: How many client accounts this reseller can have. Leave it empty for unlimited. You can change it later in the list below.
resellers.maxAppsHelp: How many apps the reseller and all their clients can have in total. Leave it empty for unlimited.
resellers.maxAiHelp: AI uses shared by the reseller and all their clients each month. When they run out, AI pauses for all of them until next month. Leave it empty for unlimited.
resellers.colAiHelp: AI actions used this month by the reseller and all their clients together, out of their monthly limit. Click a number to change the limit.
resellers.colDomainHelp: The reseller's own web address, where their clients sign in. “Not verified” means they haven't finished the setting at their domain company yet.
resellers.signInAsHelp: Opens the reseller dashboard as this reseller, to help them or check their setup. Anything you change happens in their account.
resellers.inviteLinkHelp: Makes a new invitation link for them to set their password, valid once for 7 days. It's also emailed if email is on.
resellers.resetLinkHelp: Makes a link for them to choose a new password, valid once for 2 hours. It's also emailed if email is on.
resellers.suspend: Suspend (signs out the reseller and all its clients)
resellers.suspendHelp: Signs the reseller and all their clients out at once, and stops them signing in until you reactivate. Nothing is deleted.
resellers.reactivateHelp: Lets the reseller and all their clients sign in again.
resellers.deleteHelp: Removes this reseller. Their clients keep their accounts and apps but become your direct customers on the Free plan; the reseller becomes a normal user. Can't be undone.
resellers.changeLimitHelp: Used so far, out of the limit. Click to change the limit; leave it empty for unlimited.
resellers.deletePromptOne: Delete reseller "{name}"? Their client keeps their account and apps and becomes your direct customer (on the free plan). Type the reseller name to confirm:
resellers.deletePromptMany: Delete reseller "{name}"? Their {count} clients keep their accounts and apps and become your direct customers (on the free plan). Type the reseller name to confirm:
resellers.partnerCardBody: Give a reseller's own software a key to create its clients' accounts, sign them in and build apps for them. Keys are made, rotated and revoked under Partner API.
resellers.partnerCardLinkHelp: Create, rotate or revoke partner keys, for one reseller or for the whole platform.

planPrices.title: Plans and prices
planPrices.body: Set what each plan costs per month. Leave a price empty to hide that plan. The Free plan is always there. What each plan includes is set under Plans & limits.
planPrices.planNameHelp: The name shown on the pricing and Billing pages, and on the plan in your Stripe account.
planPrices.priceHelp: What this plan costs each month. Leave it empty to stop selling it. A change only affects new subscriptions; people already subscribed keep their old price.
planPrices.currencyHelp: The currency this plan is charged in. Like a price change, it only affects new subscriptions.

stripeHelp.customers: Stripe is the payment service that charges cards. Money from your customers goes straight into your own Stripe account.
stripeHelp.clients: Stripe is the payment service that charges cards. Money from your clients goes straight into your own Stripe account.

connected.customers: Connected. Customers pay you directly; the prices are created and updated in your Stripe account when you save.
connected.clients: Connected. Your clients pay you directly; the prices are created and updated in your Stripe account when you save.

notConnected.customers: Connect your Stripe account so customers can pay. Until then, your prices still show, and checkout opens once Stripe is connected.
notConnected.clients: Connect your Stripe account so clients can pay. Until then, your prices still show, and checkout opens once Stripe is connected.

planPrices.secretHelp: The secret key from your Stripe account. It lets this server create your plans in Stripe and open checkout. It's kept hidden; leave the box empty to keep the saved one.
planPrices.secretWhere: In Stripe: Developers → API keys → Secret key. Use a test key (sk_test_…) to try it out first.
planPrices.webhookHelp: A webhook is how Stripe tells this server that someone paid, upgraded or cancelled, so their plan changes here. It's normally set up for you when you save.
planPrices.webhookAuto: Advanced: payment updates (webhook) · set up automatically when you save
planPrices.webhookBody: Stripe tells this platform when someone pays, upgrades or cancels, at this address. It's set up for you; only if that fails, add it in Stripe (events: checkout.session.completed and customer.subscription.created, updated, deleted) and paste its signing secret here.
planPrices.copyWebhookHelp: Copies this address, to paste into Stripe if you need to add the webhook yourself.
planPrices.webhookSecretHelp: Only if automatic setup failed: paste the signing secret Stripe shows for the webhook you added. It starts with whsec_.
planPrices.saveHelp: Saves your plans and prices. With Stripe connected, it also creates or updates them in your Stripe account.
